notes: How this part was researched: the session's web-search allowance ran out after six searches, so the rest was done by opening pages directly with the kit's own User-Agent: county sites, the North Dakota Court System's county and judge pages, the state's sheriff list (post.nd.gov), the Legislative Branch's biography pages, the Democratic-NPL's own candidate pages, two campaign sites, and a voter guide (theballotbrief.com) used only to find campaign site addresses.

Nothing found, left blank: Lyle Kenner, Andrew Krauseneck, Liz Braun, Gordon A Dexheimer, Steve Cottingham, Meredith Childress, Kevin Bishop, Angela (Angie) Eagle. The county pages for Emmons, Grand Forks, LaMoure, McIntosh, McLean and Pierce name other people in those offices today, so these six appear not to hold them now; no site was found for Sioux County, and ransomcountynd.com did not answer.

No page of the North Dakota Republican Party listing or endorsing its 2026 legislative or statewide candidates was found (ndgop.org has no candidates page), so no endorsed_by is recorded for Shawn Kessel, Kylan Klauzer, Scott Wagner, Brad Bekkedahl or Drew Wrigley. No campaign site was confirmed for Wrigley, Wagner, Bekkedahl, Drury or Spilman.

The Dem-NPL's legislative page links Kelly Spilman's 'Website' to bismanleaders.com, which is the Bismarck/Mandan Dem-NPL's site, not her own, so it is recorded as a party page and not as a campaign website.
Shawn Kessel's own_words is an endorsement by a person (the Governor), not a party; the second reader should judge whether it belongs. His city administrator posts have no years on the page.

Verifier (2026-10-02): every url re-opened with the kit's own User-Agent; all 34 findings confirmed on the page. Corrected: the post.nd.gov remarks in the Fisher and Jurgens sources were dropped (that list was not a recorded url and was not re-opened); Schwab's office now says the 2022 date is the current term's start. The three Dem-NPL endorsed_by entries rest on the party's own candidate lists, which present these people as the party's 2026 candidates without the word endorse; kept with that said in the unit. Kessel's own_words is a heading on his own site, five words, naming a person's endorsement, not a party's.
